title: Registered Nurse - Family Medicine
description:
Job Description:

RN - FAMILY MEDICINE
Join our Family Medicine Clinic team at ***!

Rural nursing at its finest!
You are an individual that enjoys the rapid pace of a thriving family medicine clinic and the excitement and variety of skills that come along with it.

This position is a non-exempt, full-time, benefitted position.
Anticipated schedule: MondayFriday, approximately 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.
A sign-on bonus is available for permanent, full-time hire.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide professional nursing care to patients in the clinic/outpatient setting in compliance with professional practice standards.
  • Promote a collaborative, interdisciplinary approach towards patients, families and all members of the care delivery team.
  • Use the nursing process to assess, plan, implement and evaluate patient care needs. This includes assessing patients condition, triaging patient phone calls, counseling patients, providing patient education, taking patient histories, perform screenings, and administration of vaccinations and medications.
  • Document patient care in the healthcare record according to established standards.
  • Ensure own professional effectiveness through education and professional development.
  • Participate in the development of and maintains established policies, procedures and objectives; quality improvement; safety; environmental and infection prevention programs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum requirements:

  • Graduate of an accredited school of nursing.
  • One year of experience as a registered nurse preferred.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of and ability to apply age specific principles of growth and development and life stages to meet each patients needs.
  • Current Utah Registered Nurse licensure
  • Ability to multi-task effectively in a fast paced work environment.
  • Strong critical thinking skills and ability to problem solve independently.
  • Able to lift/move up to 20 lbs. without assistance and lift/move weights beyond 20 lbs. with assistance.

This job description is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to the job.

Why Should You Join the Team at ***?

We have an amazing team here at ***, with a skilled group of healthcare providers and physicians from a wide range of specialties who are committed to the greater Moab community.

Caring for our People: Every healthcare professional that works here at MRH in both a clinical and non-clinical setting cares about our patients because these are our friends, neighbors, and our family.

Employee Satisfaction: *** strives to balance care for the community with care for its employees and offers a supportive work environment, competitive total compensation packages, and the flexibility to enjoy what makes this desert region one of the most unique and special places to live.

We offer:

  • Wide range of benefits, including:Medical Insurance
    Mental health coverage for entire family
    Retirement 403b
    Paid time off
  • Collaborative and supportive workplace
  • Professional growth opportunities including continuing education, trainings, and more!

Nestled at the base of the LaSal Mountains and along the banks of the Colorado River, small-town friendliness coupled with unparalleled natural beauty make this a great place to call home. Thanks to its perfect climate, Moab offers year round recreation opportunities, and is renowned for mountain biking, rock climbing, jeeping, hiking and river activities. description:
Job Description:

Hospice RN at Grand County Hospice

At Grand County Hospice, we are committed to providing compassionate, high-quality end-of-life care to our patients and their families. As a leader in hospice care, we believe in treating every patient with dignity and respect in their preferred place of care usually in their home.

We are seeking a dedicated and compassionate Hospice Registered Nurse (RN) to join our interdisciplinary team. The RN will provide skilled nursing care and support to terminally ill patients and their families in accordance with the patients plan of care and hospice philosophy.

Key Responsibilities:

· Perform comprehensive assessments of patients needs and coordinate individualized care plans.

· Provide pain and symptom management consistent with the hospice plan of care.

· Educate and support patients and families regarding the disease process, self-care techniques, end-of-life issues, and the hospice philosophy.

· Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team including physicians, social workers, chaplains and volunteers.

· Participate in on-call rotation

· Maintain accurate and timely documentation in compliance with state, federal, and organizational policies.

Qualifications:

· Current Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of Utah or compact state RN license.

· Minimum of 3 year of nursing experience, preferably in hospice, home health or palliative care.

· Strong clinical assessment skills.

· Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.

· Compassionate demeanor and ability to support patients and families during difficult times.

· Valid drivers license and reliable transportation required for home visits. Mileage reimbursement *** per mile.

· Current BLS Certification

· On-Call 1-3 shifts per week, to include 3 weekends during the 13 week contract depending on staffing levels. Able to respond within 45 minutes to patient needs when on call.

· Able to work holiday

· Hospicesoft/careficient EMR experience preferred

IMPORTANT!

McLaren Northern has incorporated a strict 3 strike attendance policy to advocate for their patient population. Any RN contractor who is absent from a scheduled shift or is more than 20 minutes late for their scheduled shift 3 times will be terminated effective immediately. Situations such as a communicable disease or hospitalization with supporting evidence will be reviewed in favor of the contractor. This policy will begin on 6/1/2024.



The Cardiovascular Registered Nurse uses clinical judgment skills to diagnose and treat patient responses to actual or potential health conditions. The RN is a critical member of the Cardiovascular Unit (CVU) which cares for over 4000 cardiology patients annually; procedures including PTCA, stents, TAVR, MitraClip and bi-ventricular pacemakers. Approximately 300 open heart surgery patients (18-24 hours post-op) are discharged from this unit. The CVU also specializes in the care of patients with congestive heart failure and electrophysiology studies. Our NISUS research department manages many national clinical trials using CVU.
The CVU has been awarded a Silver level Beacon Award in 2014 and was redesigned in 2017 by the American Association of Critical Care Nurses (AACN). This accomplishment represents one of many significant milestones on CVU's journey to optimal outcomes and exceptional patient care that could not be achieved without our exceptional RNs. McLaren Northern Michigan was also named a Top 50 Heart Hospital in the U.S. The leadership, medical staff, and colleagues together as a team demonstrate top performance in care, efficiency, and community value.

title: Registered Nurse - Operating Room
description:
Job Summary: As a Registered Nurse in the Operating Room at our healthcare team, you will play a vital role in ensuring the safety and well-being of surgical patients. You will collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals to deliver high-quality preoperative care, manage surgical instruments and equipment, and maintain a sterile environment. Your expertise and attention to detail will be essential in facilitating successful surgical procedures.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Preoperative Assessment: Conduct thorough preoperative assessments to ensure patients are prepared for surgery, addressing any concerns or medical history issues.
  • Surgical Assistance: Assist surgeons during surgical procedures, including passing instruments, maintaining a sterile field, and providing necessary equipment and supplies.
  • Patient Advocacy: Advocate for patient safety and comfort throughout the surgical experience, addressing any concerns or changes in the patient's condition promptly.
  • Sterile Technique: Maintain a sterile environment in the operating room, including proper sterilization of instruments and adherence to infection control protocols.
  • Patient Education: Provide patients and their families with preoperative and postoperative education to ensure understanding and compliance with care plans.
  • Documentation: Accurately document all patient care activities, assessments, and interventions in accordance with facility policies and regulatory standards.
  • Team Collaboration: Collaborate closely with surgeons, anesthesia providers, surgical technologists, and other healthcare professionals to ensure the smooth flow of surgical procedures.
  • Emergency Response: Be prepared to respond to emergency situations during surgery, including code situations, while maintaining composure and following established protocols.
  • Equipment Maintenance: Ensure proper functioning and availability of surgical equipment and instruments, reporting any malfunctions or deficiencies promptly.
Qualifications:
  • Current Registered Nurse (RN) licensure in state of practice
  • Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) preferred
  • Certification in perioperative nursing (CNOR) preferred
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in perioperative nursing or operating room setting
  • Strong understanding of surgical procedures and aseptic techniques
  • BLS and ACLS certification required
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities
  • Attention to detail and strong organizational skills
Benefits:
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
  • Access to ongoing training and development programs.
  • Supportive and collaborative work environment.
  • Meaningful work that makes a difference in patients' lives.

title: Registered Nurse – Med Surg / Telemetry
description:
We are seeking a dedicated and skilled Registered Nurse to join our Med/Surg (Medical/Surgical) unit. The Registered Nurse will play a crucial role in providing high-quality and compassionate care to patients with various medical and surgical conditions. The ideal candidate will possess strong clinical skills, excellent communication abilities, and a passion for delivering patient-centered care.

Travelers may be scheduled for rotating day/night shifts based on operational need. Preferred shifts will be honored when possible.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide direct and comprehensive care to patients admitted to the Med/Surg unit, including those with medical and surgical diagnoses.
  • Assess patients' physical and psychological needs, create individualized care plans, and implement nursing interventions accordingly.
  • Administer medications, monitor vital signs, and manage patients' pain to ensure their comfort and safety.
  • Collaborate with the interdisciplinary team, including physicians, therapists, and other healthcare professionals, to develop and implement a coordinated care plan.
  • Monitor and interpret patients' conditions, recognizing any changes and taking appropriate actions, such as notifying physicians or initiating interventions.
  • Document patient assessments, interventions, and outcomes accurately and in a timely manner using electronic health records.
  • Maintain a clean and organized patient environment, adhering to infection control and safety protocols.
  • Monitor patients requiring cardiac telemetry and respond promptly to changes in cardiac rhythms.
Qualifications:
  • Minimum 18 months of recent Med/Surg Telemetry RN experience (travel experience acceptable).
  • Minimum 18 months of permanent RN experience in the specialty prior to traveling.
  • Active Ohio RN license or compact RN license in hand at time of submission.
  • AHA BLS, ACLS, and NIHSS certifications (required).
  • Strong clinical assessment and critical thinking skills.
  • Willingness to work every other holiday as needed.
  • Must complete and pass ECG rhythm recognition and SafeMedicate assessments during orientation.
Benefits:
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
  • Access to ongoing training and continuing education.
  • Collaborative and supportive clinical environment.
  • Meaningful work delivering high-quality care in a nationally ranked health system.
